item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79797-8

item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79416-6

Here authors rationally design a lithium coordination compound BuLiPro. Compared with conventional lithium carbonate, BuLiPro improves brain lithium bioavailability, enhances GSK-3β inhibitory potency and reduces nephrotoxicity. In female AD mouse models, BuLiPro mitigates tau and amyloid-β pathologies and rescues cognitive deficits, showing potential for safer lithium-based therapeutics.

item.title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
item.description:
Klara Gregorova, Geert-Jan Will, Pia Burkard, Marcel Romanos, Andrea M. F. Reiter
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79292-0
Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

item.title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
item.description:
Yuchen Yang, Chen Ma, Jiangbin Hong, Weiming Huang, Ming Lin, Jianting Zhang, Wenhua Chen, Nanzhi Zheng, et al.
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79521-6
Abstract The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp 2 -hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

item.title: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
item.description:
Maiki Tamura, Qingci Zhao, Yusuke Yamaguchi, Manami Yasuda, Fumiyoshi Ishidate, Takahiro Fujiwara, Noritaka Nishida
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79476-8
Abstract Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

item.title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
item.description:
Kening Gong, Li Jiang, Siyang Qiu, Xueai Li, Ming Cheng, Xiaoran Tang, Changhao Yan, Lijia Guo, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79646-8
Abstract Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

item.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
item.description:
Martin Schön, Oana P. Zaharia, Christian Binsch, Huishu Lin, Claudia H. T. Tam, Cadmon K. P. Lim, Gechang Yu, Klaus Strassburger, et al.
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79351-6
Abstract Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort ( N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) ( N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, P log-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, p log-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c ( p AUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant ( p = 0.035) and age-related ( p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

item.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
item.description:
Robert Wong, Michael H. McCullough, Tianfeng Lu, Shuyu I. Zhu, Geoffrey J. Goodhill
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79123-2
Abstract Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

item.title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
item.description:
Thomas Guest, Ryan T. Fansler, Gianluca Prezza, Gohar Mädler, Hannah Schlauch, Wenhan Zhu, Alexander J. Westermann
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79554-x
Abstract Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B . thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

item.title: An explainable deep-learning framework for predicting multisystem outcomes in comorbidity-free MASLD
item.description:
Tao Yuan, Yihang Shen, Wei Chen, Chenxiang He, Zhijun Ding, Shanshan Chen, Huayi Zhang, Jinhuan Liu, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79594-3
Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with hepatic and extrahepatic morbidity, but non-invasive tests provide indirect, largely cross-sectional risk estimates, limiting continuous and individualised prognostication. Here we develop AEGIS-MASLD, an explainable deep learning framework integrating dual-stain liver biopsy images, clinical data and longitudinal lifestyle records to predict 13 MASLD-related multisystem outcomes. This retrospective multicentre study included 814 adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD without baseline comorbidities, followed for a median of 203 months. The model was developed in 546 patients from three Chinese centres using five-fold cross-validation and externally validated in 268 patients from six independent centres. In external validation, the model predicted 12 non-fatal outcomes with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.766–0.867, outperforming conventional histological and non-invasive fibrosis scores. All-cause mortality was evaluated separately using pathology and laboratory data. Annual risk estimates for non-fatal outcomes were updated as lifestyle exposures changed. Tissue analyses identified 24 histopathological phenotype clusters, linking fibrotic clusters to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, and inflammatory clusters to cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that digital pathology analysis of routinely obtained biopsy material, combined with clinical and lifestyle data, could support individualised multisystem risk assessment and follow-up in patients with MASLD undergoing biopsy-based evaluation.

item.title: Chip-scale narrow-linewidth optical parametric oscillators
item.description:
Yi Sun, Fuchuan Lei, Carlos E. Osornio-Martinez, Yan Gao, Dawson B. Bonneville, Meindert Dijkstra, Sonia M. Garcia-Blanco, Victor Torres-Company
Nature Communications, vol. 17, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79427-3
Abstract Continuous-wave-pumped optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide an exciting avenue to generate coherent radiation at wavelength regions that are difficult to reach by traditional semiconductor optical amplifiers. However, attaining ultra-narrow linewidth operation in OPOs requires pump lasers with exceptional purity to begin with. Here, we demonstrate an integrated Kerr nonlinear OPO featuring an integrated external cavity based on ultralow-loss silicon nitride that results in a continuous-wave signal with a 15-fold intrinsic linewidth reduction compared to the pump, down to 10 Hz. Our numerical analysis indicates that the intrinsic linewidth can be reduced below the Schawlow-Townes limit of a single-cavity OPO depending on the feedback length and strength of the external cavity. Utilizing an integrated erbium-doped waveguide amplifier, we further demonstrate sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth coherent oscillation. These results establish an effective pathway towards chip-scale ultra-coherent light sources with high power and broad wavelength tunability, opening new opportunities for high-precision optical sensing and detection.

item.title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79338-3

T regulatory cells (Treg) cells may be involved with the regulation of immune responses in psoriasis. Here, using psoriasis samples from humans, the authors characterize the function of CD1a-responsive Treg cells in psoriasis and show that these cells secrete IL-10 in response to lysophosphatidylcholine and are found in close proximity to CD1a+ antigen-presenting cells and are potentially dysfunctional in psoriasis.
